Q: Python packages installation - pandas & nympy A:

You're using python3.14 but this _multiarray_umath.cpython-313-darwin.so suggests that numpy is looking for a cpython built for version 3.13. I suggest creating a virtual environment to further isolate the issue. Try using python 3.13 and do clean pip installs of pandas/numpy within the venv to see if it's still throwing the error.

Q: Tensorflow 2.4.0 Cannot dlopen some GPU libraries A:

python install tensorflow==2.4.0 is not the right code to install tensorflow.

You can install tensorflow using pip command or conda command (if you have installed conda software) in your system after installing python.

To install tensorflow using pip or conda in conda environment.

  • Open the anaconda command prompt after installing anaconda/Miniconda in you system

  • Create a conda VirEnv - tf and install tensorflow after activating the VirEnv

    conda create --name tf python=3.9
    conda activate tf
    pip install --upgrade pip

    pip install tensorflow #or
    conda install tensorflow

Please follow all the software requirements to enable Tensorflow GPU support in your system and add them to bin directories to your PATH.

  • Then install the CUDA, cuDNN with conda and install tensorflow.

    conda install -c conda-forge cudatoolkit=11.2 cudnn=8.1.0
    pip install "tensorflow-gpu<2.11" #TF 2.11 not supported for GPU setup

Now you can verify if you've installed TensorFlow successfully.

import tensorflow as tf
gpus = tf.config.experimental.list_physical_devices(device_type='GPU')
cpus = tf.config.experimental.list_physical_devices(device_type='CPU')
print(gpus, cpus)

Note : Please make sure you have installed the right CUDA and cuDNN compatible to the installed Python and TensorFlow version in your system as per this tested build configuration.

Q: Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined - React-Rails A:

React-rails gem uses webpacker, so I would follow their documentation to make sure you source your environment variables correctly, particularly the portion involving the setup of dotenv files if you don't use webpack-dev-server:

Environment variables are supported out of the box in Webpacker. For example if you run the webpack dev server like so:

FOO=hello BAR=world ./bin/webpack-dev-server

You can then reference these variables in your JavaScript app code with process.env:

console.log(process.env.FOO) // Compiles to console.log("hello")

You may want to store configuration in environment variables via .env files, similar to the dotenv Ruby gem.

Here is what you could do to support a "Ruby-like" dotenv:

yarn add dotenv

// config/webpack/environment.js

...
const { environment } = require('@rails/webpacker')
const webpack = require('webpack')
const dotenv = require('dotenv')

const dotenvFiles = [
  `.env.${process.env.NODE_ENV}.local`,
  '.env.local',
  `.env.${process.env.NODE_ENV}`,
  '.env'
]
dotenvFiles.forEach((dotenvFile) => {
  dotenv.config({ path: dotenvFile, silent: true })
})

environment.plugins.prepend('Environment', new webpack.EnvironmentPlugin(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(process.env))))

module.exports = environment

If you'd like to pass custom variables to the on-demand compiler, use Webpacker::Compiler.env attribute.

Webpacker::Compiler.env['FRONTEND_API_KEY'] = 'your_secret_key'

Q: Test connection failed because of an error in initializing provider A:

First guess, wrong IP or wrong oracle home is being used (and thus different tnsnames.ora). The other guess, I assume the UDL file is being used in a Windows-based PC : the error might be because the COM objects that being used as provider is not installed correctly. Maybe there is a problem with MDAC (Microsoft Data Access Components), you might also need to reinstall Oracle Client with Windows Interfaces enabled in custom options.
